Pathogen Profile

Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus

Staphylococcus aureus causes a range of illnesses, from skin and wound infections to pneumonia and bloodstream infections that can cause sepsis and death. Less severe infections are common and occur outside acute healthcare settings and in the community. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is S. aureus that is resistant to the drug methicillin and other drugs of its class and is found primarily in healthcare settings, although since 2000 it has spread to the community where it has become common.

Geographic Locations

Antimicrobial resistance varies by location, driven by a number of factors, including antibiotic use and infection control practices in individual healthcare facilities, the underlying health and age of the patient population, and regional spread from nearby locations.
